# Final submission assessment — 30 October 2026

**Decision:** retain A5 and A6 as the primary submissions. A4 is defensible as a third entry with a more modest claim to significance. The final pass found two limited corrections, both now applied, and no new defect in the central theorem arguments inspected. These are contributions to specific debates, not demonstrated general breakthroughs.

This assessment concerns A5 v9, A6 v8 and A4 v10. The branch was checked at `fc363b6daf04e9c623ea773959b890623e379503`; no later Claude commit was present. Claude's completed review through `3db2bdc0e04aaed585357f9363ede9ab42ca8253` was already incorporated. The complete three manuscripts, including their appendices, were read in this submission pass. This is further review by an AI system involved in producing the work, not independent expert review.

## A5: retain as a primary candidate

The counterexample fixes the score and context and produces opposite belief verdicts at increasing credence in the tested proposition. Strict truth-directedness and order independence of the rational status of final states survive. The reversal for every positive premium, the restricted separability result, the optimizer characterization and the sufficient refinement theorem withstand the proof checks performed here.

Dorst's published §4.2 and Proposition 5 proof were re-read. The strongest objection remains interpretive: he may intend the marginal-value restrictions to be assumptions of the framework. On that interpretation the counterexample is outside the intended class. The essay explicitly distinguishes that interpretation from the unrestricted derivation and asks why those restrictions should be imposed. Its strongest contribution is this diagnosis, supported by a concrete strict-marginal countermodel; it is not a refutation of Lockeanism as a whole.

The overlap with guessing theory is substantial. The essay correctly demonstrates that Dorst and Mandelkern's score can reproduce its central pair of belief sets. Filtering, non-monotone guessing and the general concern about refinement are prior art. Skipper's published refinement discussion was checked again. The surviving increment is the score on unrestricted belief states with strict marginal truth-directedness and its precise optimizer characterization. The manuscript remains unchanged from v9.

## A6: retain as a primary candidate

The finite argument has a clear structure: relative defeat permits a harmful bet; absence of relative defeat puts the post-answer kens inside the current ken; reflexivity, transitivity and nesting then supply safety. The gappedness characterization additionally needs the stated questions to be available under the maintained statism assumption. The manuscript keeps those qualifications and treats the continuous weighing example separately.

The mapping to Deference Done Better was rechecked against the definitions of recommended strategy, Value and Weak Value and the Appendix B equivalence. Fixed tie-breaking supplies a recommended strategy for each decision problem. This supports the stated comparison, but also limits novelty: the general deference characterization is already established in that paper. A6 contributes its normality-specific characterization and the tests of three specified conditional inquiry rules.

One explanatory sentence in Theorem 3's construction was too broad. The construction establishes agreement between CEU and KDT for the present best act versus looking, and for comparisons among primitive acts. It does not establish agreement on every comparison involving the looking policy. In the essay's three-state example, exact arithmetic gives the original bet an advantage over looking of 1/2 under KDT and -9/2 under CEU. The actual best act nevertheless beats looking by 7/10 under both. Version 8 states only the required agreement. The theorem, underlying construction, displayed equations and appendix proofs are unchanged.

The philosophical conclusion remains conditional. The essay does not refute Conditional Knowledge Dominance itself, every knowledge-based decision theory, or inquiry with commitment to ignore an answer. Its contribution is to show what fails in the specified developments and what answer-by-answer evaluation gives up on costly inquiry. That is a substantive result within the chosen framework.

## A4: defensible third, weaker significance claim

The modified-definition witnesses for Suzy, Tracks and Doorbells have the same transition profile. The older definitions' blocked-tracks witness has the prevention profile plus one root returning to default. These identities support the anonymous-filter dilemma under the declared codings. The fixed-context conformity lemma also has a direct elimination-and-minimality proof: a conforming witness is reproducible by changing its roots alone.

The main limitation is not a newly found proof defect. The restricted policy class deliberately ignores distinctions that richer normality theories may use. Halpern already discusses both the preemption difficulty and the blocked-tracks failure, and Wysocki supplies a stronger obstruction for conjoined cases. The paper must earn its significance through its exact cross-model comparison and diagnosis of the information a separating policy needs.

The final pass adds one explicit antecedent. Halpern's automatic rock-throwing machine on page 85 already illustrates the reliability difficulty for a backup mechanism. Version 10 acknowledges this beside Sprinkler, explaining that the case applies the concern to a comparison with switching. This prevents the familiar reliability objection from being mistaken for a new discovery. The witness identities and conformity lemma are unchanged.

## Remaining limits and submission judgment

The published version of Good Guesses remains unavailable; the detailed comparison used the previously inspected July 2021 author draft. A fresh full-text copy of Wysocki's Conjoined Cases was not obtained; the earlier comparison remains the basis of that discussion. These version/access limits have not been relabeled as fresh full-text verification.

The broad computation suites and numerical integrations were not rerun because their formulas, examples and claims did not change. The new exact CEU calculation above checks the wording correction only. The formal claims were inspected as written proofs; finite computations are supporting checks, not proofs of unrestricted quantifiers or evidence of originality.

There is no identified reason in this pass to delay A5 or A6 for another general model review. A4 is suitable only with the narrower expectations stated above. No contest outcome or exhaustive novelty certification follows from that judgment. The PDFs and matching reports are the submission artifacts; no form has been submitted.

- Dorst et al. (2021), “Deference Done Better,” Theorem 2.2, the definition of recommended strategy, and Appendix B, especially Weak Value and Lemma B.13. [Published PDF](https://fitelson.org/ddb.pdf).
